title: Genome-wide association analyses of gestational phenotypes identify context-specific genetic effects.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GWAS Catalog API for PMID 42509370 lists 111 studies (GCST90837213-GCST90837323), all with full summary statistics, CC0 licence. FTP folders for GCST90837255 (height) and GCST90837243 (GDM, gestational diabetes) each hold one GWAS-SSF tsv.gz of 152 MB and 157 MB (over the 50 MB cap, not downloaded). A ranged read of the first 256 KB of the height file decoded 12,978 rows: 14 columns (chromosome, position, alleles, beta, standard_error, effect_allele_frequency, p_value, rsID, two-cohort Direction, N, GENE, IMPACT, Consequence), no missing values in that chunk. Metadata yaml says GRCh38, whole-genome sequencing, n=108,202. API reports about 7.28 million variants per study.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: No open full text or supplement (no PMCID; paywalled). That the individual-level data are in GSA-Human HRA006833 (controlled access), that 7.8% of variants have gestation-specific effects and 18.7% show genotype-by-timing interactions, and the 4,688 signals / 1,703 new count come from the abstract and search snippets only. The tables listing which variants are gestation-specific are in the unretrieved supplement. Units of beta (raw vs standardised trait) are not stated in the file metadata.

a1_downloadable.note: Summary statistics download openly from GWAS Catalog FTP (checked, CC0 licence). Individual-level genotypes and phenotypes are controlled access in GSA-Human HRA006833 (Genome Sequence Archive for Human, China; needs an application), per the paper's data statement only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Files hold per-variant association estimates (beta, p-value) per trait, not a per-example outcome. Any ML target worth predicting (causal variant, pregnancy-specific effect, genotype-by-timing interaction) would have to be built by fine-mapping or by matching to non-pregnant GWAS such as BioBank Japan; the paper's own context-specific calls sit in a paywalled supplement.

a3_inputs_present.note: Genomic coordinates (GRCh38) and alleles are present (checked), so DNA sequence context could be pulled from the reference genome without lookups.

a4_units_stated.note: Beta has no stated unit or trait scale in the file or metadata yaml (checked); whether quantitative traits were inverse-normal transformed is unknown without the methods.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 7.28 million variants per study per the API snp_count; not counted in the file. Independent signals (4,688) are from the abstract only.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: about 150 MB gz per trait; 111 traits about 16-17 GB gz
a6_fits_laptop.note: One trait streams easily; all 111 would exceed the 5 GB working-set guide unless filtered to significant variants.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 111 studies in the Catalog match the abstract's 111 phenotypes; the height sample size 108,202 matches the metadata. Signal counts not checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: Beta and p-value are regression estimates smeared across correlated nearby variants (linkage disequilibrium), not a per-variant measurement; usable variant labels would be fine-mapping model outputs, which is the circularity A8 warns against.

existing_models.name: GDM (gestational diabetes) prediction model combining polygenic risk score and prenatal records, Nature Communications 2025 (same NIPT cohort group)
existing_models.score_and_split: AUC (area under the ROC curve) 0.729, accuracy 0.835, for GDM before 20 weeks; split not checked (from search snippet).

backbone.name: AlphaGenome (DNA sequence model) would be the only candidate, for variant-level features
backbone.hardware: CPU for embeddings of a few thousand lead variants; untested

integration.partner_dataset: BioBank Japan female GWAS or AlphaGenome Atlas variant effects
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do pregnancy-specific genetic effects concentrate in hormone- or placenta-active regulatory DNA that sequence models can recognise?

controls.positive_control: Known height and hemoglobin loci (e.g. HBB region for hemoglobin A2/F) should top their traits.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle which variants are labelled pregnancy-specific.
controls.external_validation: BioBank Japan female GWAS for the non-pregnant comparison; none for pregnancy-specific labels.

honest_claim_h3: At best: predicts, among genome-wide significant variants in Han Chinese pregnancies from NIPT (non-invasive prenatal test) low-coverage sequencing, which ones show a stronger effect in pregnancy than in a separate non-pregnant cohort, a label we would have built ourselves.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around trait-linked variants to predict whether a variant's effect on a blood trait changes during pregnancy.
plain_idea.train_on: Lead variants from 111 pregnancy trait association studies with surrounding DNA sequence; number of usable variants unknown (4,688 signals per abstract, not verified).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the variant's effect differs between pregnancy and non-pregnant women, which would have to be computed by comparing these statistics with another cohort's; no measured label exists in the files.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Maternal-health geneticists would learn whether pregnancy-specific genetic effects have a recognisable regulatory signature; but the label is constructed, so the answer is fragile.

ml_idea: Variant-level classification of pregnancy-specific versus shared genetic effects from sequence-model embeddings; rejected because the label must be constructed across cohorts and the paper's own calls are in a paywalled supplement.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only: streaming one 150 MB gz trait file and filtering to significant variants fits in a few GB; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Obtain the supplementary table of gestation-specific variants and count how many independent variants are labelled specific versus shared; under ~400 kills it.

verdict_reason: Open data are 111 sets of GWAS (genome-wide association study) summary statistics (checked, CC0), not a labelled table; any prediction target must be constructed by fine-mapping or cross-cohort comparison (A2, A8), beta units are unstated (A4), and individual-level data are controlled access in GSA-Human HRA006833.
